items.note: Varies the share of LLM agents in mixed human-AI groups playing a collaborative description (naming-convention) game and measures convergence and content of shared expressions; borderline, since the task is communication rather than creative ideation and humans interact with AI agents rather than receive AI help, so the next stage should confirm scope.

Novice designers complete two conceptual design tasks with or without text and image generative AI; the abstract reports process stages, and search notes say N = 20 (likely below the 50 threshold) with expert ratings; Design Science version of arXiv 2502.00283.

CHI system paper comparing ChatScratch (storyboards, image generation, Scratch LLM) with plain Scratch for children aged 6-12; claims higher-quality projects, but whether project creativity is scored and the sample size are not stated.
Teaching experiment on multimodal generative AI in college English creative writing, with writing samples and questionnaires; comparison group and N not stated, and creativity may be self-reported.
Design ideation experiment comparing human-only groups with human-GenAI groups on idea quality and quantity in divergent and convergent phases; SSRN working paper, N and assignment not stated.

Quasi-experiment with 45 university art students comparing mind-mapping-integrated GenAI digital storytelling with conventional GenAI digital storytelling (AI vs AI configuration); scored story scripting, video, and theme performance plus creative-thinking tendencies; below 50 participants.

Pilot with 29 participants solving an ethical dilemma under AI-prohibited, AI-optional, or AI-mandatory conditions, with blind-coded perspective and counterargument diversity; task is ethical reasoning rather than a creative task, so scope is borderline, and N is below 50.

HCI system paper: comparative study (N = 12) of the IdeaBlocks generative design tool versus a baseline generative tool, measuring images explored and visual diversity; no no-AI arm; DIS 2026 version of arXiv 2507.22163.

Pilot RCT with 24 college students writing an essay with no, limited, or unlimited LLM access; essay quality and similarity to LLM output measured; below 50 participants; BEA 2026 version of arXiv 2606.00250.

Two intact high-school classes (31 GenAI drawing vs 29 conventional drawing) in an ancient poetry course; main outcome is learning achievement, drawings described as richer, and creativity appears as a student trait moderator, so a scored creativity outcome on output is uncertain.
